result.rule: When the description says an external device or party keeps sending back status or updates while the actor performs other work at the same time: Model the receipt of these ongoing updates as its own intermediate catch event on a branch that runs in parallel with the actor's other work, and do not omit it. Do not model it as a receive task, because the wait is for a recurring message rather than a unit of work. Join the branch back to the main flow when the work it supports completes.

When the description says an external party arrives at a time that is not fixed, and a later activity can only start after that arrival: Model the wait for the external party's arrival as an intermediate catch event placed before the activity that is performed after the arrival. Do not model this wait as a send task that forwards a request to that party, and do not model it as an ordinary task.

When The description says the process sends a request or order to an outside party and then continues only after a reply, confirmation, or status arrives, so the next decision or step depends on that reply.: Model the wait for that reply as its own step placed directly after the sending step and before the next decision or activity. Use a receive activity (bpmn:receiveTask) when receiving the reply is the unit of work, or an intermediate catch event when the wait is only a pause. Connect the send step, the receive step, and the next element with sequence flows, and do not let the flow skip from the send step straight to the decision.

When the description states that, while a piece of work is pending, the participant keeps the customer informed with status updates, or that a result such as a document or item is handed over at the end of the work, as separate steps in the sequence: Model each such stated update or handover as its own task in the sequence where the description places it (during the pending period, or after the work is completed), placed before the next step that depends on it. Do not drop it, and do not merge it into the surrounding work task, because a stated step that is missing from the model is a faithfulness error.
